purpose: Track old-account repurposing, dormant-account activation, thematic pivots, and reuse of old visual media in false/new contexts without treating account age or old footage alone as attribution evidence.

user_observation.summary: User reports manually observing long-lived accounts, with special interest in accounts created around 2014, and old YouTube material later reused with modern claims as purported evidence about past events.
user_observation.claim_limit: Specific account identities/operators remain unresolved unless independently verified.

account_age_signals.evidence: Published analysis of Internet Research Agency campaigns found many political/news accounts registered in 2013-2014 and used later; some cohorts showed multi-year lag between account creation and concentrated operational activity.
Secondary Infektion reporting documents early persona experiments beginning in 2014, including pseudo-personalities and cross-language amplification.

DFRLab identified a 2025-2026 network of YouTube channels where some accounts were years older than the current political-content campaign, including one created in 2007, suggesting possible repurposing as content farms.
Academic research on YouTube repurposed 'chameleon channels' documents a market for second-hand accounts and frequent shifts into policy-sensitive content.

media_laundering_signals.evidence: Old footage is repeatedly recycled in Russia-Ukraine information flows with changed captions, dates, locations, or actors.
StopFake documented multiple December 2014 News Front/Novorossia summaries using older YouTube footage as if it proved new events.
RFE/RL documented Russian state TV reusing footage from an earlier North Caucasus report in a fresh Ukraine atrocity claim in May 2014.
Media Forensics Hub/ProPublica found Russian-language fake fact-check videos whose metadata showed a single source file duplicated to fabricate both the alleged Ukrainian fake and its debunking.
MythDetector traced a video uploaded in November 2014 that continued circulating with changing false descriptions through later years, including 2023-2026 claims.
